name: The Inventions in Every Home
description: Soap, spectacles, zips and microwaves: the small inventions that fill the rooms we live in, and who thought of them.

checkpoints.name: Ancient comforts
checkpoints.note: Polished stone and metal mirrors, soap, candles and chopsticks are some of the oldest household goods. Spectacles and the bristle toothbrush came later but are still old.

checkpoints.name: The age of ingenuity
checkpoints.note: Inventors brought the flush toilet, the pressure cooker, matches, the sewing machine and the safety pin into homes, and shops sold them to a growing urban middle class.

checkpoints.name: Machines for the house
checkpoints.note: Dishwashers, typewriters, zips, vacuum cleaners and fridges relieved housework and office work, while safety razors and flasks changed daily habits.

checkpoints.name: The electric and plastic age
checkpoints.note: Ballpoint pens, microwaves, instant cameras and hook-and-loop fasteners filled drawers and kitchens. The Walkman and the sticky note turned small ideas into habits.
